The contract confirms four sampled failures and requires visual comparison before any policy edit. I’m now anchoring those keyframes to the inherited guidance, per-example observations/metrics, and the prefilled candidate; I’ll write the diagnosis before touching the policy.

The scalar evidence separates two failure modes: the naive fast gait is mostly swept downward and exits after 50 time units, while the 0.90-period variants move modestly upstream but curl upward, hit joint/rate limits, and still leave the domain. I’m applying the skill’s visual check now to distinguish productive upstream swimming from steering-induced curl and wake advection.

The visual sheets confirm the stronger policy’s upstream motion is self-propelled, but its useful approach ends in a large upper loop with the posterior joint and both rates/commands saturated. The inherited rate variants did not solve that: additive rate damping still saturated and exited sooner, while longer look-ahead lost upstream authority. I’ll record a sign-preserving, closing-only steering brake as the single candidate hypothesis before editing the policy, as required by the skill and workspace contract.

The candidate now preserves the only upstream-capable gait and changes just the steering-rate structure: rate can attenuate an already-closing turn but cannot add steering or flip its sign. I’m now updating the durable experience bank with the evaluated negative boundary that motivated this design; the new rollout itself will not be claimed as evidence.

The required notes, policy, and durable guidance are all updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s mandated check-runner now; it will run only the semantic-guidance, lightweight Julia contract, schema, and boundary checks—no CFD.
